correctness.rationale: Exact monomial norms give \(c_n=1/(1+a^{n-N})\). Enestrom–Kakeya and Hurwitz give zero-free \(|s|<(a^N+a)/(a^N+1)\). Shift by \(s^{-N}\); locally uniform convergence on \(a<|s|<1\) to the Ramanujan 1ψ1 product, whose factors are zero-free and winding zero on any circle in that annulus. Argument principle then counts exactly N zeroes for all large N. Radius collapse follows from varying the circle; log-derivative residue moments for \(k\ge1\) are uniformly O(1), proving angular equidistribution. The product identity and index winding were independently algebraically reconstructed. Finite numerical checks supplement, not prove, this argument.

value.rationale: A natural two-circle Hardy norm creates a nontrivial deterministic zero cloud whose cardinality grows with inner-circle mass while all underlying function spaces stay equal to \(H^2\) as sets. The exact count, explicit zero-free inner boundary, and uniform angular distribution are structural invariants motivated by recent radial reproducing-kernel questions, not arbitrary finite enumeration. The result clarifies the loss of kernel zero-free geometry under extreme interior-boundary mass concentration.
